_comment: Exemptions from the isolation-clamp completeness gate, //hdl/common/power:iso_clamp_audit_test.
Every entry is a decision, not a suppression: an output that really is a gated-to-always-on
crossing belongs in the clamp set of the generated MCU.vhd (emitted by
platform/common/python/mcu_vhd.py), never here. `files` scopes the exemption, because which
outputs a configuration leaves unconnected is a property of that configuration; `*` means every
file. A `files` entry that no instance uses fails the gate, so the list cannot go stale.

flash_mem_en.reason: Not a crossing. The SPI0 flash / XIP quartet is hart-0-only wiring: the orchestrator owns the boot flash and every hart_tile instance leaves the tile flash port unassociated, so no always-on logic samples it.

flash_clk_mem.reason: Not a crossing, same reason as flash_mem_en: the tile's flash clock has no consumer outside the tile.

flash_mab.reason: Not a crossing, same reason as flash_mem_en: the tile's flash address bus has no consumer outside the tile.

trap_flag.reason: Not a crossing on a gated tile. Only hart 0's trap_flag reaches a pin (GPIO0); a tile's is mapped `open`, so the dark domain drives nothing.

dbg_halted.reason: Argus builds no per-tile debug halt observation, so the port is unassociated there and is not a crossing. It IS a crossing on the Castalia MCU and is clamped there; this exemption is scoped so that dropping that clamp is still a failure.

tcm_ext_rdata.reason: Argus has no read-only TCM apertures, so the tile slave port is unassociated there. Clamped on the Castalia MCU; the exemption is scoped for the same reason as dbg_halted.

tcm_ext_done.reason: Argus has no read-only TCM apertures, so the tile slave port is unassociated there. Clamped on the Castalia MCU; the exemption is scoped for the same reason as dbg_halted.

always_on_instances.hdl/argus/MCU.vhd::hart0: Argus builds hart 0 out of hart_tile rather than orch_tile, and hart 0 is the always-on management hart: PWRCR bit 0 has no flop and pwr_ctrl emits no pd_* row for it, so the instance straps pd_iso_en (and pd_sleep) to '0' and its outputs never cross a power boundary.

wrapper_instances.hdl/common/orch_tile.vhd::tile: orch_tile is the hart-0 wrapper that keeps the soft core's module names disjoint from the hardened hart_tile netlist. It passes pd_iso_en straight through to its own port, and every MCU straps that port to '0' because the orchestrator sits in the always-on centre band with no power intent. The wrapper adds no power boundary of its own.
